chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the woman in Ihram who dies while she is in her menstruation. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Perfume should not touch her, even if there were women with her who were not in Ihram.'

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ الْمُحْرِمَةِ: The woman in Ihram (state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.طَامِثٌ: Menstruating (in a state of major ritual impurity)
key_terms.نِسْوَةٌ حَلَالٌ: Women who are not in Ihram (in a state of ritual freedom)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on applying perfume to a woman who dies while in Ihram during menstruation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the prohibition of applying perfume (tayyib) to a woman in Ihram who dies during menstruation is absolute, regardless of the presence of other women who are not in Ihram. This ruling underscores the specific legal status of the menstruating woman in Ihram, distinguishing her from those in ritual purity and highlighting the continuity of Ihram restrictions even after death. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the distinct juridical categories of Ihram and menstruation in burial rites.
